The other inputs to the cost of capital are on record: a risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct}, an equity risk premium of {cost_of_capital.equity_risk_premium|pct}, a pre-tax cost of debt of {cost_of_capital.pre_tax_cost_of_debt|pct} and a tax rate of {tax_rate|pct}. price_position.reading: Where the price sits in the range cannot be read, because there is no range and no price. Neither market.price nor cost_of_capital.price_at_cutoff is in the calculator. Under market.missing it prints "no price series was given: the forward track's price source is Tiingo, and without its token no series is fetched". The free-cash-flow yield that would cross-check the price is missing for the same reason. The balance-sheet side of the bridge from enterprise value to equity is on record: net debt is {ratios.solvency.net_debt}, so cash exceeds debt, and operating lease liabilities are {ratios.solvency.operating_lease_liability}. That net debt counts cash alone, {terms.cash_and_short_term_investments_now}, with no line for the retained Sandisk shares that the company plans to exchange for its own stock. A value built on operating income would carry that stake nowhere unless it were added. Without a value per share or a price, no position is stated and none is estimated.

most_sensitive.reading: Python built no sensitivity grid, because the valuation it varies was not run, so the two assumptions value is most sensitive to cannot be read off it, and no ranking is estimated here. Judged from the drivers alone, one of the two places where the scenarios disagree most is where the operating margin settles. The bear case ends it near fiscal 2022's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.3.operating_margin|pct}, earned by the combined company before the Sandisk separation. The base case ends it below fiscal 2025's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_margin|pct}, and the bull case ends it near the trailing {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct}. The record shows the margin can swing across that whole span and beyond: fiscal 2024 ran at {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.operating_margin|pct} and fiscal 2023 at {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.operating_margin|pct}.

Revenue growth in the first year is the other place where the scenarios disagree most. It sets the whole growth path, since Python fades it in a straight line to the terminal rate by year ten. The bear case starts close to fiscal 2024's trough-year growth of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.revenue_growth|pct}, on the reading that a short customer list pauses after a heavy build; the top ten customers took {concentration.facts.27.value|pct} of the quarter's revenue. The base case starts well below the trailing four-quarter growth of {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, and the bull case a little below it. No path was valued, so these files do not show how far each one moves value.

accounting_adjustments.reading: The valuation did not run, so valuation.accounting_adjustments was never computed. In any case there were no adjustments to carry: the accounting reader wrote none, and the quality-adjusted free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted} applied none and refused none. The reader gave the reason. The largest item it found, the non-cash, tax-free mark-to-market gain on the retained Sandisk shares, which MD&A describes as "a gain of $2.73 billion on our retained interest in Sandisk" in the quarter, has no amount in the calculator. It also sits below operating income, outside the operating income my drivers act on. The timing items that lifted operating cash flow have no amounts on record either. Two of the reader's findings still bear on value through the drivers rather than through an adjustment. First, Python would tax operating income at the trailing effective rate of {tax_rate|pct}, which rests partly on the tax-free Sandisk gain and on windfall benefits that will end. That is why my base terminal margin sits below fiscal 2025's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_margin|pct}, so the terminal year does not stack a peak margin on a low tax rate. Second, hedge losses held in other comprehensive income are due to reach cost of revenue within twelve months. That is why the bear case starts the margin below the trailing {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct} and the base case trims its first-year margin. The retained Sandisk shares themselves are a non-operating asset that the net debt of {ratios.solvency.net_debt}, built on cash alone, does not count.
